record.file_problem: Repo metadata, README, and file list only; result-file contents were not provided, and code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports SAE feature measurements on safety-related prompts, but does not test the difference-in-means refusal direction, its causal role, or any other listed claim version. It explicitly notes that the base model does not exhibit refusal and that causal involvement was not tested.
record.gate_note: The README reports feature selectivity and overlap for refusal, sycophancy, and jailbreak prompt categories. These are measurements of input representations, not of refusal behavior or the claimed refusal direction, so the rows are recorded with versions ["none"]. The token-position findings do not bear on a claim version and are not included.
record.test_reason: SAE feature selectivity on safety-category prompts in base GPT-2 Small. There is no difference-in-means refusal direction, no ablation or addition, and no refusal behaviour: the README says the base model doesn't exhibit refusal. So no version is tested. 'Discusses' is generous, since the repo does not mention the refusal direction at all; cites_only or T6 would fit equally well.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. GPT-2 Small SAE features distinguish safety-category inputs from controls, using largely separate feature sets per category. The authors note the base model doesn't refuse, so causal involvement is untested.
record.recipe_differences: This is an SAE feature-analysis research repo: it measures feature selectivity and overlap on safety-related prompts, rather than finding a harmful-minus-harmless residual direction and causally ablating or adding it. The README describes no causal intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports that selectivity increases with depth from layers 3 to 9 and varies by prompt category; it notes that sycophancy prompts share a distinctive syntactic pattern that may inflate selectivity.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-9 top-10 SAE feature mean selectivity: refusal 9.0, sycophancy 17.4, jailbreak 6.3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In GPT-2 Small, SAE features separate safety-category prompts from benign controls to different degrees.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-30 feature sets per category have Jaccard overlap of 0.00–0.03 at layer 9.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In GPT-2 Small, the SAE features most selective for refusal-trigger, sycophancy and jailbreak prompts are nearly disjoint.

fits_no_version.finding: Selectivity rises from layer 3 to layer 9 across categories.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In GPT-2 Small, SAE feature selectivity for safety-category prompts grows with depth.

record.problems: The README says the model is base-only and does not exhibit refusal, so causal involvement in safety decisions cannot be tested. It reports a small prompt set (50 safety prompts and 30 controls), notes that sycophancy selectivity may be inflated by shared prompt syntax, and acknowledges imperfect SAE reconstruction. No uncertainty estimates or statistical-significance results are reported in the README.
record.rows_left_out: Token-position descriptions were omitted because they do not bear on a claim version or add a relevant measurement of the refusal direction. The README also names four features that did not fire above threshold in the 20-prompt position-analysis subsample, but that result concerns position analysis rather than the claim.

untested.parts: All of it: no refusal direction, ablation, addition, or capability check.
Jailbreak prompts were only used as an input category; there is no suppression or adversarial-training test.
Feature-set overlap across prompt categories is not a geometry of refusal.
Category features in a model that doesn't refuse cannot separate harm judgment from the refusal decision.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are correctly linked to none and cannot_determine. R6's refusal layer-3 value is not stated in the README and might be in results/data/safety_features.json, which was not read. The paper does not cite the original source.

versions.untested_parts: The causal effect of ablating or adding a difference-in-means refusal direction, and preservation of other abilities, were not tested.
No weight edit or practical refusal-removal test was reported.
No attack suppression of the direction or training against its ablation was tested.
The study compares SAE feature sets across safety prompt categories, not alternative geometries or multiple directions underlying refusal.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision representations were tested.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer was tested.
No refusal-training procedure or training stage was varied.
